new.s: What is the term for the rate of birth of individuals in a population, expressed per unit population per unit time?
new.x: Natality means births in a population; its rate is given per unit population per unit time, not per female.

new.s: What is the largest population that an environment can support for ever called?
new.x: Carrying capacity is the largest population an environment can sustain; the S-curve levels off at it (K).

new.s: Producers, consumers and decomposers together form which aspect of an ecosystem?
new.x: Producers, consumers and decomposers form the structure of an ecosystem; the food chain is its dynamic (functional) part.
new.angle: U0763 #19 Ecosystem structure vs function (PYQ y806c503ddd9 dynamic part)

new.s: What is the living biomass present in a trophic level per unit area at a given time called?
new.x: Standing crop is the amount of living biomass at a given time; productivity, by contrast, is a rate.
new.angle: U0763 #5 Ecological pyramids -> biomass/standing crop (PYQ yb767c3b31f5)

new.s: Rhizophora, a mangrove plant growing on saline coasts, is an example of which group of plants?
new.x: Rhizophora grows in saline coastal soil, so it is a halophyte.

new.s: Which of the following are adaptations of halophytes?
new.x: Halophytes such as mangroves have breathing roots (pneumatophores), vivipary and salt glands.

new.s: Who coined the term 'ecology' in 1866?
new.x: Ernst Haeckel coined 'ecology' in 1866; Tansley coined 'ecosystem' in 1935.

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Rule)
A. Bergmann's rule
B. Allen's rule
C. Gloger's rule
List-II (Trait)
1. Colouration
2. Body size
3. Length of ears and limbs
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Bergmann's rule is about body size, Allen's about ears and limbs, and Gloger's about colouration.

new.s: Who coined the term 'biological diversity'?
new.x: The term 'biological diversity' was coined by Raymond F. Dasmann.
new.angle: U0763 notes gap: Dasmann -> biological diversity

new.s: Which of the following is a coevolved plant-pollinator pair?
new.x: The yucca plant is pollinated only by the yucca moth; the two have coevolved, like the fig and fig wasp.
new.angle: U0763 #9 Biotic interactions -> coevolved pollinator pairs

new.s: What are organisms that can tolerate only a narrow range of temperature called?
new.x: Stenothermal organisms tolerate a narrow temperature range; eurythermal ones tolerate a wide range.
new.angle: U0763 notes gap: stenothermal vs eurythermal

new.s: Where was the Ramsar Convention on wetlands signed in 1971?
new.x: The convention was signed on 2 February 1971 at Ramsar in Iran, hence its name.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ramsar Convention:
1. It imposes punitive sanctions on countries that damage listed wetlands.
2. India became a party to it in 1982.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Ramsar Convention is not regulatory and has no punitive sanctions; India joined it in 1982.

new.s: Which of the following defines a biome?
o: A large region marked by its climate and dominant vegetation
Individuals of one species in an area
A transition zone where two communities meet
All the ecosystems of the Earth together
new.x: A biome, such as tundra, desert or rainforest, is a large region defined by climate and dominant vegetation.

new.s: What is the actual range of conditions and resources used by a species under competition called?
new.x: The realised niche is the part of the fundamental niche a species actually uses when competitors are present.
new.angle: U0763 #11 Habitat vs niche -> realised niche

new.s:
Which of the following is the correct sequence of Clements' phases of ecological succession?
1. Invasion
2. Nudation
3. Stabilisation
4. Reaction
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Succession starts with nudation (bare area), then invasion, competition, reaction and finally stabilisation (climax).
new.angle: U0764 #12 Stages of succession -> nudation to stabilisation sequence

new.s: Which is the main reservoir of nitrogen in the nitrogen cycle?
new.x: About 78% of air is nitrogen gas, so the atmosphere, not the soil, is the main reservoir of nitrogen.
new.angle: U0764 #13 Biogeochemical cycles -> main reservoir (PYQ y6a697d4ac77)

new.s: Which of the following statements about the functions of the environment is NOT correct?
o: It sustains life through biodiversity and the ozone layer
It provides aesthetic services such as scenery
new.x: The environment supplies both renewable and non-renewable resources, so 'only renewable' is wrong.
new.angle: U0764 #10 Functions of environment -> which is not (PYQ y518c061856c, y0c70f3e5892)

new.s: Apart from nitrogen-fixing organisms, which natural process fixes atmospheric nitrogen that reaches the soil with rain?
new.x: Lightning turns atmospheric nitrogen into compounds that rain carries to the soil, adding to its nitrogen.
new.angle: U0764 #14 Nitrogen cycle -> processes adding N to soil (PYQ y42415e41a68)

new.s: What would happen to mineral cycling if all decomposers were removed from an ecosystem?
o: Nutrients would stay locked in dead matter and not return to the soil
Energy would begin to cycle back to producers
Minerals would return to the soil faster
new.x: Decomposers break dead matter into simple nutrients; without them minerals stay locked in dead organisms.
new.angle: U0764 notes gap: removing decomposers blocks mineral cycling (APPSC 2025)

new.s: Which bacteria carry out denitrification?
new.x: Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus turn nitrate back into nitrogen gas; Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter carry out nitrification.

new.s: In which year did the UN release the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment?
new.x: The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (2005) grouped ecosystem services into four categories.

new.s: In which season are dust storms most common in north-west India?
new.x: Dust storms in Rajasthan and north-west India are most common in the hot, dry pre-monsoon months, peaking in May.
new.angle: U0765 #16 Sand and dust storms (PYQ y5c2b2a5fbc4)

new.s: What is the full form of UNCCD?
o: United Nations Commission on Climate and Development
United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
United Nations Convention on Climate Change and Drought
United Nations Council for Combating Desertification
new.x: UNCCD stands for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, adopted in Paris in 1994.
new.angle: U0765 #5 UNCCD (PYQ y5924ee7d8c8, y6f6d4b22772 full-form angle)

new.s: What is the full form of LDN, the target under SDG 15.3?
new.x: LDN means Land Degradation Neutrality, that is, no net loss of land health by 2030.

new.s: In which village did Gaura Devi lead women to save trees during the Chipko movement in 1974?
new.x: Gaura Devi led the women of Reni village in Chamoli in 1974, a key event of the Chipko movement.

new.s: Where is the secretariat of the UNCCD located?
new.x: The UNCCD was adopted in Paris in 1994, but its secretariat is in Bonn, Germany.

new.s: As per FAO FRA 2025, what is India's rank in the world in annual gain in forest area?
new.x: FRA 2025 ranks India 9th in forest area and 3rd in annual gain of forest area.

new.s: Which soil-conservation method grows strips of grass between crops to break the force of wind?
new.x: Strip cropping leaves strips of grass between crops to break wind force; shelter belts use rows of trees.

new.s: The Global Land Outlook is the flagship publication of which body?
new.x: The Global Land Outlook (2017, 2022) is the flagship report of the UNCCD.

new.s: What is the main purpose of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974?
o: To prevent and control water pollution and maintain or restore the wholesomeness of water
To levy a cess on water used by industries
To regulate groundwater extraction by farmers
To supply drinking water to rural areas

new.s:

2. It was set up in 1976 under the Air Act, 1981.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: APPCB's head office is at Vijayawada; it was set up in 1976 under the Water Act, 1974, as the Air Act came only in 1981.
new.angle: U0766 #13 APPCB -> head office, setting up

new.s: Under the Doon Valley notification (1989), industries burning more than how much coal or fuel a day were not allowed?
new.x: The Doon Valley notification under the EPA barred industries burning over 24 MT of coal or fuel a day.

new.s: What is the jail term for offences under the Water Act, 1974?
new.x: The Water Act provides 1.5 to 6 years' jail; up to 5 years is the original EPA penalty.
new.angle: U0766 notes gap: Water Act penalties

new.s: For which purpose was the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 enacted?
o: Insurance cover for forest land diversion
Compensation to farmers for crop loss
Funding of State Pollution Control Boards
Relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances
new.x: The PLI Act, 1991 gives relief to people hit by accidents while handling hazardous substances.
new.angle: U0766 #1 Environmental Acts -> PLI Act purpose

new.s: For what purpose was the National Green Tribunal set up?
o: Effective and speedy disposal of cases on environmental protection and conservation of forests
new.x: The NGT was set up to decide environmental and forest cases quickly; standards and consents are the work of pollution control boards.

new.s: In Common Cause (2017), what did the Supreme Court order mining firms in Odisha that mined beyond their environmental clearance to pay?
o: 50% of the value of the illegally mined mineral
10% of the value as a token penalty
100% of the value of the illegally mined mineral

new.s: The National River Conservation Plan covers pollution abatement in how many rivers?
new.x: NRCP covers 38 rivers in 16 States, outside the Ganga basin.
